facebook.long_form:
Moving day arrives at Black Desert Resort, and the Bank of Utah Championship has set up a Saturday with real intrigue.

Heading into Round 3, Rory Ostrander leads at -15 after rounds of 65-66. Four players are within two strokes. The most compelling subplot: defending champion Shane Ostrander sits T-3 at -13, two back from his older brother Rory.

It's the kind of leaderboard golf fans love on a Saturday morning — no runaway leader, a defending champion in contention, and Scottie Scheffler lurking at -11 with two rounds to find something.

Round 3 tee times begin this morning at Black Desert. The leaders go off in the afternoon local time. If the leaderboard holds tight through the back nine today, Sunday should be exceptional.

stories.title: LIV Golf October 13 Deadline — 12 Days Away, DeChambeau Still Undecided
stories.angle: Where does the deal stand with 12 days left, and who still hasn't committed?

x_posts.label: Post 3
x_posts.text: 12 days until LIV Golf's October 13 deadline. DeChambeau still hasn't committed publicly. At least 6 marquee players remain undecided. Players who sign get 52.5% equity. The clock is running. #LIVGolf #PGATour

x_posts.label: Post 4
x_posts.text: The LIV Golf player deadline is Oct. 13. That's 12 days from now. The deal offers 52.5% equity to signing players. DeChambeau — LIV's biggest name — hasn't said yes or no yet. #Golf #LIVGolf

facebook.long_form:
Twelve days.

That's how long is left before the October 13 deadline for players to decide on LIV Golf's merger framework. The deal, as structured, offers participating players a 52.5% equity stake in the combined entity — a figure that would make them among the most financially empowered athletes in professional sports.

And yet several high-profile names haven't committed.

Bryson DeChambeau — arguably the most recognizable face in LIV Golf — has not publicly announced his position. Sources indicate at least six marquee players remain undecided as the deadline approaches.

The October 13 date isn't soft. It was set publicly, accepted by the relevant parties, and carries the weight of a process that has already been running for months. What happens after it passes — whether extensions are possible or whether non-signers fall outside the framework — isn't entirely clear.

We're 12 days out. The next 12 matter.

---

article.headline: The LIV Golf October 13 Deadline Is 12 Days Away — And Several Key Players Still Haven't Decided

stories.title: LOTTE Championship Tees Off in Hawaii — Korda Chases Back-to-Back
stories.angle: Can Korda maintain her dominant stretch, and who has the form to challenge at Hoakalei?

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: The LOTTE Championship tees off in Hawaii. Nelly Korda is in the field looking for back-to-back wins. Thitikul, Tavatanakit, and Lydia Ko also competing at Hoakalei CC. LPGA's Hawaii week is here. #LPGA #LOTTEChampionship

facebook.long_form:
The LPGA Tour heads to Hawaii this week for the LOTTE Championship at Hoakalei Country Club in Ewa Beach — and the field assembled at one of golf's most scenic venues is as strong as the fall schedule gets.

Nelly Korda arrives as the headliner after winning three of her last six starts on tour. A victory at the LOTTE would extend a stretch of dominance that's been the defining story of the LPGA's second half of 2026.

The competition isn't short of quality. Patty Tavatanakit, Atthaya "Jeeno" Thitikul, and Lydia Ko are all in the field. Thitikul, who reached world No. 1 earlier this season, has been knocking on the door in recent weeks.

The $2.1 million purse is part of the LPGA's premier fall stretch. Hoakalei's oceanfront layout adds a visual dimension that few venues on any tour can match.

Round 1 is underway today. Full coverage all week.

stories.title: Defending Champion Ostrander's Title Defense Is On — He's T-3 After 36 Holes
stories.angle: Brothers on the same leaderboard at the same event, with the title on the line.

x_posts.label: Post 6
x_posts.text: Shane Ostrander won the inaugural Bank of Utah Championship at Black Desert last year. This week, his brother Rory leads the field. Shane is T-3, two shots back. Title defense vs. family. #PGATour

facebook.long_form:
Here's a storyline you don't see in professional golf very often:

The defending champion at the Bank of Utah Championship is Shane Ostrander. The current leader — two strokes ahead heading into Round 3 — is Rory Ostrander. Shane's older brother.

Shane won the inaugural edition of this event at Black Desert Resort last year. This week, Rory came out posting 65-66 over two rounds. Shane, playing his own tournament, fired back with 67-65 and sits T-3.

The gap is two shots. The leader boards show Ostrander at the top twice. One wants to defend. One wants to take something his brother built.

Whatever happens Sunday, this is the week's most compelling personal story.

---

article.headline: Defending Champion vs. His Brother: The Ostrander Storyline That Owns Moving Day at Black Desert

stories.title: International Team Has Lost 11 Straight Presidents Cups — What Changes Now?
stories.angle: What structural changes could actually shift the balance, or is the talent gap simply too wide?

x_posts.label: Post 7
x_posts.text: Team International has lost 11 consecutive Presidents Cups. The last win was 1998 at Royal Melbourne. USA just won again in Medinah, 17-13. The next Presidents Cup isn't until 2028. Something has to change. #PresidentsCup #Golf

x_posts.label: Post 8
x_posts.text: The Presidents Cup International team hasn't won since 1998. That's 11 straight losses. USA won again at Medinah. Trevor Immelman has two years to figure out what changes. Does anything actually fix this? #Golf

facebook.long_form:
The International team in the Presidents Cup hasn't won since 1998.

That was Royal Melbourne. The International side beat the United States 20.5-11.5, a result so dominant it felt like a turning point for the event. Instead, it became the last chapter of a competitive era that has not returned.

Eleven consecutive losses followed. The most recent, 17-13 at Medinah just days ago, extended the streak into a territory most team sports competitions never reach. USA has won every Presidents Cup of the 21st century.

Trevor Immelman will lead the International team into the 2028 edition. The challenges are structural: the International side draws from players outside Europe and the United States, meaning its pool lacks the organizational depth of Ryder Cup-calibrated European players. The selection process, the preparation timeline, the captains' pick philosophy — all have been questioned after every defeat.

What changes now? Golf Fanrecap takes a look at what would actually need to be different in 2028 for the outcome to have any chance of being different too.

article.headline: The International Team Has Lost 11 Straight Presidents Cups. What Would Actually Change That?
